Title: CBH's FY26 orderbook target raised to RM800mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) has raised CBH Engineering Holding Bhd's financial year 2026 (FY26) orderbook replenishment assumption to RM800 million from RM600 million, supported by its stronger-than-expected data centre (DC) pipeline.
The company's year-to-date replenishment stands at RM482.7 million, following the latest win of an RM88.1 million contract.
PublicInvest also lifted FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts by an average of 17 per cent.
The firm raised its target price for CBH to RM1.16, based on 20 times FY27 earnings per share and maintained its "Outperform" call.
CBH Engineering Sdn Bhd, CBH's wholly-owned subsidiary, secured the RM88.1 million design-and-build contract for a 275kV consumer landing station serving a DC in Selangor.
The project covers design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning, with works commencing on Aug 13 2026 and targeted for completion by 12 May 2027.
PublicInvest estimated the contract will contribute RM13.2 million over its duration, assuming a mid-teen profit margin.
The latest win lifts CBH's outstanding orderbook to RM891.7 million with over 90 per cent attributable to DC-related projects.
Its tenderbook remains healthy at RM1 billion, about 80 per cent of which is DC-related, providing strong visibility for future replenishment.
PublicInvest remains positive on CBH's growth prospects, underpinned by structural DC tailwinds and accelerating hyperscaler AI spending.
Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta are collectively committing over US$600 billion in 2026, supporting continued DC build-out in Malaysia.
While grid delivery capacity remains a near-term constraint, this could play to CBH's electrical infrastructure expertise, PublicInvest said,
Its expansion into BESS and other segments should further diversify revenue streams over time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Anwar notices graduate's speech inspired by his own, jokes about 'royalties'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A young graduate who drew inspiration from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's speech for his own graduation address has caught the attention of the man himself.
Awwal Azzuddin, who received the Highest Award at Kolej Permata@Pintar, took to Threads to share how Anwar's keynote address at the PKR 2026 National Congress had inspired his speech at the college's graduation ceremony.
"I did not copy it word for word. I simply learned from someone I admire. I learned from Datuk Seri's speech," he wrote.
Awwal also said he hoped to meet Anwar one day and have the opportunity to share his story with him.
His post, which has attracted more than 11,000 likes, soon caught Anwar's attention.
View on Threads
"Congratulations on your award and keep up the good work. It was a good speech. Maybe I should charge you a little in royalties," Anwar wrote.
Awwal replied: "Thank you, Datuk Seri! As for the royalties, perhaps we can discuss them when we meet in person."
The exchange has since drawn praise from social media users, with many congratulating Awwal and encouraging him to continue pursuing his ambitions.
One user, @Deedanii0, said Anwar was among the politicians from whom people could learn a great deal, particularly through his speeches.
Another user, @Fairoznasha, wrote: "Young people are the future of the nation. Keep it up and continue inspiring others!"
Meanwhile, Zirahnad said: "Congratulations, Awwal! I hope that one day you will become prime minister, just as you have always dreamed. Wishing you continued success!"

Title: Pas-Umno unity possible if parties willing to compromise on seats, says Pas spiritual leader
Article:
ARAU: Political cooperation between Pas and Umno can be achieved if the two largest Malay-based parties compromise on seat allocations ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said reviving ties between the two parties is nothing new as they have cooperated before, adding that Malay voters want to see the partnership continue.
He said the unity can be realised if challenges surrounding seat distribution for GE16 are resolved amicably through sincerity and a willingness to sacrifice.
"I see seat allocation as something that will not be a problem. What matters is that both parties must be sincere in this cooperation and be prepared to make sacrifices," Hashim said when met here yesterday.
"Pas has sacrificed a lot in previous collaborations, and as a result, we are now closer to leading. The opportunity for unity between Pas and Umno is wide open, and we only need to nurture it.
"I am also confident the public has long awaited the cooperation between the two largest Malay-Muslim political parties. The current political climate clearly requires Pas and Umno to work together."
[[nid:1528000]]
Earlier, the 72nd Pas Muktamar in Kelantan on Saturday made Muslim unity its primary agenda heading into GE16, sending a clear signal that the party intends to strengthen political cooperation centred on Malay-Muslim interests.
However, Pas election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor previously insisted that the party must defend all the seats it won in the last general election.
The Kedah Menteri Besar said giving away potential winning seats to other parties while taking on high-risk seats would be considered "sincere and foolish".
Meanwhile, commenting on internal friction within Pas in Perlis, Hashim advised that the matter be resolved as soon as possible.
"To resolve or clear up the issue in Perlis, Pas central leadership must look into the root cause of the problem.
"This issue has been raised for a long time, and I hope it receives attention from the central leadership," he said.

Title: Fire at Bidor FRIM forest, operation resumes this morning
Article:
IPOH: About 2.42ha of forest area at the Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM) in Bidor caught fire in an incident yesterday evening.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said his department received a call about the fire at 5.42pm before a team of personnel from the Bidor Fire and Rescue Station was rushed to the location.
He said the operation was carried out using a 700-foot jet stream with two jets and a transport pump which sourced water from a nearby pond.
"The operation continued last night with a change of personnel at the location.
"The fire was put under control and only 15 per cent of the burning area remains," he said in a statement.
He said the operation was suspended at midnight due to safety factors and the condition of the fire that would not spread.
The operation resumed this morning.

Title: Ringgit opens almost flat vs greenback amid ongoing west Asia conflict
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit was almost flat against the US dollar at Tuesday's open, as investors remained cautious amid the ongoing West Asia conflict, which continued to drive crude oil prices higher and support the greenback.
At 8 am, the local currency inched up to 4.0420/0480 against the greenback from Monday's close of  4.0440/0485.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the continued conflict suggests US inflation may remain above the US Federal Reserve's two per cent target for a prolonged period.
"In that sense, talks of a US interest rate hike next week are gaining momentum against a backdrop of strong non-farm payrolls (NFP) outturn last week," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said the agreement between Iran and Oman to manage shipping through the Straits of Hormuz, now in its final stage, indicates that the conflict with the US could persist for an extended period.
"This could mean a prolonged conflict with the US will result in higher crude oil prices in view of the ongoing disruptions to oil supplies from the Gulf region, which represents about 20 per cent of global oil supplies.
"However, we do see the ringgit will maintain its tight range posture as the positive macroeconomic backdrop domestically provides the compelling reason to stay long in Malaysian financial assets. Hence, the US dollar-ringgit could range between RM4.04 and RM4.05 today," he said.
Meanwhile, Quintex Intel global strategist Stephen Innes said a stronger US consumer price index (CPI) reading could bolster the case for a September Fed interest rate hike and provide short-term support for the US dollar.
"A number of analysts have started leaning more aggressively in that direction, although markets are still essentially pricing the September decision as a coin toss," he said.
The ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
It slipped against the Japanese yen to 2.6272/6313 from 2.6173/6204 at Monday's close, fell versus the euro to 4.7000/7070 from 4.6991/7044, and eased vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4753/4834 from 5.4736/479 previously.
However, the local note traded mostly higher against regional currencies.
It gained against the Thai baht to 12.2995/3246 from 12.3041/3231 at the previous close, edged up versus the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.47 from 6.46/6.47, and inched up vis-a-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 229.1/229.5 from 229.2/229.6, yesterday.
The ringgit inched down versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1945/1997 from 3.1943/1981, previously.

Title: Trump threatens to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier's US sales unless it builds locally
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened Monday to block US sales of Canadian plane maker Bombardier unless it builds aircrafts in the country, complaining of "unjust and unfair" bilateral trade provisions as he escalates a tariff war.
The angry social media post marks the second stunning potential move by the US leader this year against the manufacturer, which has thousands of its aircraft currently operating in US airlines' domestic fleets.
And it comes on the eve of Canada imposing retaliatory tariffs on a range of US goods beginning Tuesday.
"No more selling Bombardier in the United States!" Trump posted in all caps on his Truth Social platform, although he did not specify how he would achieve a sales halt.
"If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a 'piggybank.'"
"Canada blocks our GREAT American Banks, and Companies" from doing business there, Trump added. "That Era is OVER!"
The US market accounts for more than half of Bombardier's revenue, Trump said.
Back in January, furious over what he said was Canada's refusal to grant certification to new models of US-made Gulfstream jets, the president threatened to decertify Bombardier planes in the United States and impose a 50-per cent tariff on Canadian aircraft.
Those threats apparently were never carried out, but Trump said Canada quickly certified Gulfstream planes the following month because of his intervention.
Trump's social media post Monday signaled continued acrimony over Bombardier, amid a broiling bilateral tariff fight.
Even if Trump sought to follow through on his latest threat, it remained unclear how it would happen. The Federal Aviation Administration, not the White House, is the US agency that certifies or decertifies aircraft in the country.
Bombardier models remain US certified and the company is currently exempt from US tariffs. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment about Trump's post.
Last month, as trade negotiations collapsed, Trump slapped 50-per cent tariffs on some US$20 billion worth of Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to cement.
Canada announced it is imposing retaliatory tariffs on a similar amount of US products beginning early Tuesday.
The duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent will apply to imports from the United States covering steel and aluminum products as well as dairy goods like cheese.
Negotiations between the two sides broke down late last month after days of meetings in Washington, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney saying he decided to suspend the trade talks.
At the time, Carney said the Trump administration's terms were ultimately unacceptable, and that US negotiators had introduced restrictions on Canadian trade deals with other countries at the eleventh hour.
US officials also made unacceptable "threats" to the French language and "Quebec culture," he added, referencing the French-speaking province in eastern Canada.
Ottawa and Washington have not resumed negotiations since, and have continued trading barbs.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal disaster: Malaysian families seek answers over search areas, DNA samples
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians who remain uncontactable following landslides and floods at the Nepal-Tibet border want the government to clarify the 'last known locations' being used to guide search efforts by the SMART team.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said families were seeking an immediate and detailed explanation on whether the government had obtained new information on the last known locations of the missing Malaysians.
Masfih is a support group for families of those who have become uncontactable following the disaster.
"Does the government now have information or coordinates on the last known locations of Malaysians that differ from those provided by their families?" he said in a statement today.
He said yesterday's update said the
SMART team
would be deployed to conduct reconnaissance in areas believed to be linked to the last known locations of Malaysians who remained uncontactable.
However, Manivannan, whose sister Komathi is among those uncontactable, said none of the 55 Malaysians was reported to have a last known location in the area being searched by the SMART team.
"If the government has new or different information on their last known locations, families must be informed immediately.
"This is not merely a technical issue. It directly affects the direction of the search operation and, most importantly, the fate and safety of our family members," he said.
He also questioned why such critical information had not been shared with families, who had provided authorities with details on the missing Malaysians' movements, last communications, locations and chronology of their disappearance.
He also sought clarification over what he described as discrepancies in the collection and processing of
DNA samples
from the families.
"If all 55 samples had been collected on Sept 5 as stated by the (foreign) minister, why was one family member still scheduled to provide a sample on Sept 7?
"We need accurate and consistent facts, not information that keeps changing," he said.
Manivannan said families were not merely members of the public waiting for media statements, but the immediate relatives of the missing Malaysians who possessed crucial information that could assist search operations.
"After almost two weeks, it is deeply disappointing and increasingly frustrating that basic information with direct implications for the search operation remains unclear to families," he said.
He urged the government to provide specific answers on the last known locations being used by the SMART team, the source and basis of the information, the areas being searched and the rationale behind the operation.
He also called for a clear explanation on the discrepancy involving the 55 DNA samples.
"We are not asking for special treatment. We are only demanding transparency, accurate information and proper explanations on matters involving the safety and fate of our family members," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Human rights activist Beverly Joeman dies at 56
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human rights advocate and former Bersih Sabah vice-chairperson Edlyn Beverly Joeman died today. She was 56.
Beverly died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu after battling acute myeloid leukaemia. She is survived by 3 children.
She served as Bersih Sabah vice-chairperson from 2016 to 2023.
"Beverly was a steadfast activist who championed justice and fought against oppression. She was someone who loved all people regardless of their race or religion.
"Throughout her life, she remained committed to defending human rights and protecting the vulnerable," Bersih said in a statement today.
Former Bersih chairman Thomas Fann, who worked alongside Beverly for more than 12 years, described their partnership as one rooted in shared values and genuine friendship.
"I think we found in her a kindred spirit. Someone who shared the same love of the country and aspiration for the rakyat.
"We wanted to build a Malaysia that is respectful of each other's fundamental rights regardless of ethnicity or religion," Fann told the New Straits Times.
After leaving Bersih in 2023, Beverly and Fann co-founded Projek Sama (Project Stability and Accountability for Malaysia) in 2024 alongside other former Bersih members.
Fann said he last saw Beverly three months ago at his brother's funeral, where she had travelled from Kota Kinabalu.
"We noticed she looked tired and a bit off-colour. We told her to get a check-up when she returned. It was right after that they found out she had leukaemia," he said.
Despite her diagnosis, Beverly pursued treatment, and those close to her believed her strength and optimism would see her through.
"We thought that she could beat it, knowing her strength, character and her optimism. But we never expected that the disease would take her so quickly, in less than 3 months. So that was the last time I saw her," Fann said.
Meanwhile, Tenaganita executive director Glorene Das remembered Beverly for her warmth and infectious presence.
"She was so much more than the positions she held. Sabah has lost one of its passionate daughters.
"Bev was a courageous activist, a committed advocate for justice, and a powerful voice for Malaysia's Indigenous communities, particularly in her beloved Sabah," Das said in a Facebook post today.
Bersih extended its condolences to Beverly's family and paid tribute to the legacy she left behind.
"The entire Bersih family extends condolences to Beverly Joeman's family.
"Thank you for your kindness and the path you paved for activism. May she rest in peace," the group said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix continues to pursue MYEG Philippines, this time through IPVG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The saga for the acquisition of MyEG Ventures Inc continues with Zetrix AI Bhd announcing a new deal to acquire a 50 per cent stake in MyEG Ventures Inc for RM130 million from IPVG Employees Inc.
The deal comes on the same day Zetrix AI announced the termination of a deal with Next Lion Ltd, which was first announced on Sept 1.
Within three days, Zetrix AI announced the deal with Next Lion, terminated it and announced a new deal with IPVG Employees.
This calls into question whether Next Lion was ever an interested party for the deal in the first place, or whether the aim is just to consolidate the accounts of MyEG Philippines Inc, a 51 per cent subsidiary of MyEG Ventures.
It also calls into question whether Zetrix AI is setting a psychological floor price for the group's shares, which has seen its value plunging over 60 per cent between Aug 26 and Sept 4, that caused more than RM3 billion of market cap to evaporate.
Zetrix AI said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia last Friday that it entered into a share purchase agreement with IPVG Employees on Sept 4 to buy 15.25 million shares in MyEG Ventures, representing a 50 per cent stake.
The RM130 million consideration will be satisfied through the issuance of 360.57 million new Zetrix AI shares at 28 sen each, valued at RM100.96 million, and RM29.04 million cash funded through its own funds.
The issue price represents a 4.1 per cent discount to Zetrix AI's five day volume weighted average market price of 29.21 sen up to Sept 3, the last trading day before the issue price was fixed.
MyEG Ventures holds a 51 per cent stake in MyEG Philippines. Zetrix AI currently owns a direct 49 per cent interest in MyEG Philippines.
The proposed acquisition will give it an additional 25.5 per cent indirect interest through MyEG Ventures, raising its effective interest in MyEG Philippines to 74.5 per cent. This means MYEG Philippines will become a subsidiary of Zetrix AI, with its financials consolidated into the group.
It was the same objective when Zetrix AI announced the first deal involving Next Lion. The difference is in the vendors, as Next Lion, being the 50 per cent shareholder of MyEG Ventures, is no longer part of the deal.
Next Lion is wholly owned by Yap Shon Leong, the chief executive officer of M&A Value Partners Asset Management Malaysia Sdn Bhd. M&A Value Partners is owned by M&A Equity Holdings Bhd.
Also, the current deal fixes the issuance price for the share portion of the consideration, which effectively provides a minimum valuation for Zetrix AI.
After the deal was announced, Zetrix AI's share price jumped two sen or 5.88 per cent to 27 sen.
Questions sent to Zetrix AI were not answered as at press time.
A MORE CONVOLUTED DEAL
Under the initial terms with Next Lion, Zetrix AI would also issue up to 360.6 million new shares, with the remaining balance to be funded via cash payments. However, the price for the new issuance of shares was not fixed.
Zetrix AI said the deal was terminated due to its share price volatility. Between Sept 1 and 4, the counter was traded between 17 sen and 30 sen band.
However, the five day volume weighted average market price of Zetrix AI up to and including Sept 4 is 27.43 sen, not far off from the 28 sen fixed for the new deal with IPVG Employees. This shows that the difference in the two deals are merely the vendors, rather than the deal.
The current arrangement also meant that IPVG Employees must first buy a 40.6 per cent interest in MyEG Ventures from the other minority shareholders, before the deal is completed.
Zetrix AI did not state how much IPVG Employees is paying for the 40.6 per cent interest.
IPVG Employees itself is a minority shareholder in MyEG Ventures, holding only 9.4 per cent stake. The largest shareholder of the company is Next Lion with 50 per cent, followed by IP Ventures at 16 per cent.
Besides IP Ventures, the other minority shareholders are Shennan A Sy, Edward Derrick P Chiongbian and Kaikaku Fund LP. Zetrix AI listed Jaime Enrique Y Gonzalez as the controlling shareholder of IPVG Employees with 99 per cent stake.
STRENGTHENING PHILIPPINES PRESENCE
It is not known whether IPVG Employees and IP Ventures are related. Once the deal goes through, IPVG Employees will own 4.28 per cent stake in Zetrix AI.
A quick search reveals that Gonzalez founded Intellectual Property Ventures Group (IPVG), a technology company in the Philippines, in 2004, before its assets spun off into IP Ventures in 2012.
Zetrix AI said the proposed acquisition intends to strengthen its presence in the Philippines, broaden its business operations and customer base and support its longer term expansion plans in the region.
Zetrix AI said MyEG Philippines' revenue and profit had increased over the past five years, while its growth prospects were supported by financial projections for the next five years.
Its earnings per share stood at PHP0.82 as of Dec 31, 2025, compared with PHP0.31 two years earlier.
The deal values MyEG Philippines' at 62 times its net profit for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2025 of RM2.08 million (or PHP32.27 million).

Title: Flight data recorders recovered from Amazon cargo plane crash
Article:
MIAMI: Officials have recovered the flight data recorders from an Amazon cargo plane that overran the runway in Miami and slammed into two vehicles, killing five people, authorities said Monday.
One of the vehicles struck in Sunday's accident was a cleaning-services van carrying seven people on airport property, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) chief Jennifer Homendy said.
The jet then tore through a perimeter fence, bashing an SUV traveling on a public road and hitting a second fence line separating an area where robotaxis were parked, she said.
While Homendy refused to discuss the health status of the plane's two pilots, she said the victims were limited to the people in the two vehicles that were struck.
"We do want to interview the crew," she said. "As we speak, recovery operations continue."
Homendy described a "devastating" scene at Florida's busiest airport, where hundreds of flights were delayed as investigators began probing the crash site and emergency responders continued to recover the remains of some of the victims in the accident.
"We were able to recover the flight data recorder and the cockpit voice recorder," which were being sent to the NTSB for analysis, she said.
"The investigation and access to the aircraft as well as evidence can wait while the recovery operation goes forward," Homendy said. "That is most important, reuniting families with their loved ones."
She said the plane was a Boeing 767 made in 1994 and operated by 21 Air LLC, based in Miami and contracted to Amazon. It was on its third flight of the day, and was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico.
"In total, it was about 400 meters past the paved surface" when the plane finally came to a halt, she said, adding that she walked the full length of that path beyond the runway.
"There's debris everywhere," along with spilled fuel and fuel inside the aircraft that needs to be removed, Homendy said.
"The Econoline van is torn apart," she said, referring to the first vehicle hit. "It certainly must have been devastating."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2.7 billion exposed to second-hand smoke as deaths hit 1.6 million: Study
Article:
PARIS: More than 2.7 billion people including children have been exposed to second-hand smoke globally, contributing to nearly 1.7 million deaths in 2023, according to study published Tuesday in The Lancet.
Tobacco remains a leading cause of disease globally, the study said, noting many "non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke" were among the estimate total of 8 million people who died in 2023 of smoking-related illnesses.
"Exposure to second-hand smoke is a globally recognised health risk, with no safe level of inhalation," it said.
By reviewing studies published in the US National Institutes of Health database PubMed along with population surveys, Tuesday's study sought to estimate the prevalence of exposure to second-hand smoke and quantify the burden of disease in 204 countries and territories between 1990 and 2023.
Among the approximately 2.7 billion people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023 were 767 million children aged 0 to 14, the study found.
This exposure is estimated to have resulted in 1.66 million premature deaths and causing premature disability and illness, leading with ischemic heart disease, a heart condition caused by insufficient oxygen supply to the heart muscle.
In children, exposure to second-hand smoke is estimated to have caused 5.2 million respiratory tract infections in 2023, it said.
People in proximity to someone lighting up are exposed to both the "sidestream smoke" from the burning tobacco product and smoke exhaled by the active smoker, the study explained.
"The sidestream component, which dominates the air non-smokers breathe, is unfiltered... carrying higher per-unit concentrations of the toxic and carcinogenic compounds" than that being inhaled by the active smoker, it said.
Despite significant declines in smoking prevalence globally since 1990, the absolute number of people exposed has remained stable due to population growth and increased exposure in Africa and the Middle East.
Women are also disproportionately affected by second-hand smoke, particularly in regions where smoking prevalence among women is low, it noted.
"Despite this substantial burden, (second-hand smoke) exposure remains rarely acknowledged as a major risk factor for female health," it said.
The study called for governments to implement stronger tobacco controls in public places and in homes in order to better protect women and children from second-hand smoke.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal rescuers focus on 121 hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched on Monday for more than 100 hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels days after four miracle rescues from the wreckage of catastrophic floods that laid waste to towns and villages on the Himalayan border with China.
The rescues have offered a glimmer of hope as Nepal marked the 13th day after the disaster, traditionally the final day of mourning in Hindu rites, for the hundreds killed in the floods.
About 121 of a total 900 people missing from the hydroelectric projects could have been trapped in these tunnels, army rescuers said. Others may have been working elsewhere at the power plants but not inside the vast network of tunnels.
Among those whom rescuers were trying to find on Monday were four out of six people missing at the Chilime hydropower project in the hard-hit Rasuwa district who could still be alive, Shri Ram Neupane, a lawmaker involved in rescue efforts, told Reuters.
Authorities had obtained specialised equipment and identified techniques needed for the Chilime operation, Neupane said. Rescuers believe that there could be survivors trapped inside tunnels because many have air pockets, as well as spaces and rooms for people to stay, they said last week.
In recent days, search teams in Nepal have rescued four people, including a Chinese national who was pulled from a tunnel on Saturday. The others were two hydropower workers rescued from another tunnel on Friday and a Nepali woman pulled out from her buried house on Saturday.
Government offices in the Hindu majority country and at missions abroad would fly the national flag at half-mast to mark the 13th day after death, the home ministry said in a statement. The day is considered the final day of mourning by the faithful, who commemorate it with rituals and food offerings.
The disaster was triggered on August 26 when a huge mass of mud and rock, following the collapse of part of a glacier, crashed into a river along the border between Nepal and China's Tibet region. The resulting floods washed away towns and villages and buried roads and highways under mud and debris.
At least 1,380 people have been killed by the mudslide and more than 5,500 are missing in Nepal and Tibet.
Nepal has asked the international community for urgent supplies, including high-capacity drones, Bailey bridges, DNA testing kits, tunnel rescue suits, and items for epidemic prevention, the foreign ministry said in a statement.
WILL PROMPTLY SHARE INFORMATION, CHINA SAYS
Chinese officials said on Sunday that workers had recovered 12 more bodies as the search continued for hundreds still missing in Tibet. Many among the missing are Indians or people of Indian origin who were in the area in connection with trips to the Lake Mansarovar and Mount Kailash in Tibet, holy Hindu pilgrimage sites.
"The Chinese side will continue to make every effort to conduct search-and-rescue operations and handle post-disaster matters," foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a press briefing.
China has faced pressure from some families of foreign visitors missing in Tibet, who say they have struggled to obtain information on missing relatives.
Mao said Beijing would promptly release "updated information on the disaster situation and rescue activities." On Sunday, China for the first time invited journalists from eight foreign media outlets, including Reuters, to visit the core affected areas.
With search teams still looking for survivors, Nepal's government has not planned any wider events for the final day of mourning.
"There are no government programmes organised as the rescue and search operation is still going on in the flood-hit areas," Phanindra Paudel of the National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) told Reuters.
President Ram Chandra Paudel, the ceremonial head of state, was touring flood-hit areas on Monday and would survey damage caused by the disaster, his aide said.
Security personnel at the district jail in Nuwakot, one of the two worst affected districts, saved 923 prisoners by shifting them to a building in a higher location before flood waters entered their low-lying building on August 26, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post.
Authorities also captured 50 prisoners who had broken the prison wall and gates as flooding began, and had fled barely 100 metres, Shah said on Monday.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN holds advantage as Melaka election arithmetic shifts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   With Melaka edging closer to a state election, the political arithmetic is shifting, with Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan and Perikatan Nasional weighing their options ahead of a possible dissolution of the state assembly by the end of the month.
BN goes into the contest from a position of strength after winning 21 of the state's 28 seats in 2021, but analysts say its choice of electoral strategy — whether to go it alone or work with another bloc — could determine the size of its victory.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia's Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said BN remained well placed to retain the state even without an alliance, but cooperation with PH could maximise its gains.
"PH would be more beneficial to BN if the objective is to maximise the number of seats, particularly by avoiding three-cornered contests," he told the
New Straits Times
.
He said PH's strength in urban and non-Malay-majority areas complemented BN's support in rural and Malay-majority constituencies.
A BN-PN pact, meanwhile, could consolidate Malay support but would be harder to negotiate as both blocs compete for similar seats and could risk alienating non-Malay and moderate voters.
"Winning Malay votes alone may not be enough to win Melaka," he said.
Universiti Teknologi Mara political analyst Dr Ariff Aizuddin Azlan said BN's established support base meant it could retain the state on its own.
He added that  PN's strongest prospects remained in Malay-majority seats and PH would remain difficult to dislodge in DAP-held Chinese-majority constituencies.
[[nid:1527963]]
He said three-cornered contests could benefit either side, depending on where opposition votes were split.
Universiti Sains Malaysia's Professor Datuk Dr Sivamurugan Pandian said BN remained the frontrunner, but cautioned against using the 2021 result as a direct benchmark.
He said Malay support, younger voters and turnout would be crucial, with the outcome ultimately hinging on which coalition could avoid splitting its own vote bank.
"Melaka's  election is not merely about who is strongest, but who is most successful in preventing their own votes from being split," he said.
The calculations have been complicated by developments on the ground, including DAP's withdrawal of support for the Melaka government and Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh's warning that he would not contest if BN entered an electoral pact with PH.
With the possible dissolution drawing closer, the question is no longer simply who can win Melaka, but who can put together the most effective electoral formula.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal mourns as families pray missing loved ones are still alive
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepal held a national day of mourning with candlelight vigils on Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive.
The Aug 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,399 people, with more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners.
Flags flew at half-mast and hundreds of people gathered for the vigils in the Nepali capital Kathmandu, as the nation marked the 13th day after death in line with Hindu mourning rituals.
Hundreds of hydropower workers are among the missing, but the rescue of three of them from deep inside tunnels – two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday – have buoyed hopes that more could still be alive.
Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts were continuing at "the same tempo" to make sure "that no one is still stranded."
Entire communities have been swept away, with roads destroyed and homes demolished.
[[nid:1527956]]
- 'HOPE' -
But families of some of the missing workers who gathered in Kathmandu said the government must move faster.
"We have a lot of hope," said Reena Amatya Shrestha, whose brother is among the missing.
"They say they are doing rescue. If the rescue is there, where's the result? We need the result."
Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said the operation presented an unprecedented challenge.
"We are facing something I have never faced before," said Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, in a post on social media.
"Not one rescue, but multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties, and lives that may still be saved."
Foreign experts, including from China, India and South Korea, are aiding Nepali teams in rescue efforts.
"We are measured not only by the lives we save, but by the lives we refuse to abandon," said Dix.
Drone pilot Adarsha Raj Bhusal recalled sinking into mud after leaping from a helicopter into the flood-ravaged Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa district days after the disaster.
"The moment I landed I sank into the mud up to my waist," the 24-year-old told AFP on Monday in Nuwakot district.
"Other soldiers were there to help, but they were struggling just as much as I was. That's how bad the conditions were... it was intense the entire way in."
- 'NEW LIFE' -
Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel visited relief camps in Nuwakot, speaking to those left homeless by the disaster.
"Today the entire nation is mourning this horrific disaster," he said in a statement.
"To everyone waiting for news of family members and friends, I want to assure you that search and rescue operations will continue."
With mortuaries overflowing, Nepal has buried hundreds of bodies in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, according to police.
Despite the gloom, there have been remarkable tales of survival.
Chandika Shrestha, a 64-year-old Nepali woman, was pulled out alive from her mud-covered home in Bidur on Saturday.
Her family had already held a symbolic funeral ceremony, believing her dead.
"Chandika has got a new life," her neighbour Buddhi Lal Dongol told AFP. "It would be so good if the others who are missing also came back."
Several families held last-rite ceremonies in Nuwakot to mark the 13th day of mourning, while Buddhist monks held prayers for the dead.
"I have had to hold myself together a lot," 63-year-old Kula Priya Nepal, whose son was killed at a hydroelectric project, told AFP.
While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melting worldwide, increasing the risk of such disasters.
Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, has said reconstruction could cost billions of dollars.
Its economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale.
The disaster has come just ahead of the anniversary of last year's Sept 8-9 mass anti-corruption protests that toppled the government.
Rescuers have retrieved 1,356 bodies in Nepal, while around 4,994 people are missing, according to the disaster agency.
The toll in China stands at 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media.
On Monday, local volunteer groups in Kathmandu packed utensils, blankets and clothes to be distributed to survivors.
"As Nepalis, we've always been told that you look after your people," volunteer Ashim GC told AFP.
"And these are our people." --AFP

Title: Melaka election looms as parties ramp up poll preparations [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Political parties are already putting their election machinery through its paces as Melaka edges towards a possible state election, with Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh hinting that the assembly could be dissolved by the end of the month.
Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the party was preparing to defend its four existing seats while seeking further gains, with discussions on candidates and election machinery already under way.
"He can dissolve the state assembly at any time. As for us, we have already made preparations to face the election," the Kota Melaka assemblyman told the New Straits Times.
Khoo said discussions within DAP and with its Pakatan Harapan partners had been ongoing and would continue regardless of when the assembly was dissolved.
"We have always been having discussions. It is not as if we only discuss things after the dissolution. The discussions have already been taking place," he said.
Meanwhile, Perikatan Nasional component Wawasan is also preparing for the possible contest.
Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah said the party was identifying potential candidates, training its election machinery and studying constituencies it wanted to contest.
"As a party member of PN, we certainly want to contest this election under the PN banner," he said.
Saifuddin said Wawasan was also assessing candidates it believed could win, while any decision on the electoral formula or cooperation would be left to its president.
Pas Central Ulama Council chief Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party's machinery was likewise ready, although no formal election meeting had been held.
"For now, there has been no official meeting on this. Generally, Pas' machinery is already prepared," he said.
For Umno, vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said political parties should always be ready for an election, regardless of when it was called.
"All parties must always be prepared. An election is an opportunity to regain the people's mandate," he said.
Khaled said the factors influencing public support would determine the coalition's position, with the target previously set by Melaka BN remaining its benchmark.
BN won 21 of the 28 state seats in the 2021 election, while DAP secured four and Bersatu and PKR took the remaining three.
Rauf's latest signal has now put the parties on notice, with the contest likely to turn on more than just the number of seats each bloc currently holds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia names Toba Pulp Lestari suspect in alleged US$113mil tax fraud case
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Attorney General's Office (AGO) named listed pulp producer Toba Pulp Lestari as a suspect in a case involving alleged tax fraud which resulted in a state loss of around 2 trillion rupiah (US$113 million).
The AGO last month named two tax officers as suspects for allegedly accepting bribes from Toba Pulp Lestari. Both, identified by prosecutors only by their initials, were tax audit supervisors for Toba Pulp Lestari between 2020 and 2024.
Toba Pulp Lestari did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Saiful ​Bahri Siregar, director of investigations at AGO's special ​crimes unit, told reporters that prosecutors alleged under-invoicing by Toba Pulp Lestari between 2008 and 2025.
Toba Pulp Lestari is alleged to have violated an anti-corruption clause in Indonesia's criminal code, he said.
Prosecutors allege Toba Pulp Lestari changed and manipulated a system code where a product should have been classified as dissolving pulp but was reported as another lower-value product, Siregar said.
Prosecutors also allege Toba Pulp Lestari submitted tax reports that were not in accordance with the actual transactions, he added.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC to meet e-commerce platform operator over drug sale
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will meet an e-commerce platform operator over the alleged online sale of drugs.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had expressed concern over the new sale tactics.
"I have instructed the MCMC to meet the operator of one platform that we believe is being used to sell drugs such as fentanyl and a substance known as 'piu-piu'."
He said this at the opening of a strategic cooperation workshop involving the Rural Community Centres (PKD) under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry and the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) here yesterday.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, his deputy Datuk Rubiah Wang and MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.
Fahmi said efforts to expand Internet access, including in rural areas, must be accompanied by measures to ensure communications networks remained secure and were used responsibly.
He said online scams and other forms of abuse could flourish if digital security and literacy among users were not strengthened.
"We provide good Internet access and complement it with PKD and Nadi facilities because we want to bridge the gap between rural, suburban and urban areas.
"However, if these communications networks are not secure and users lack the knowledge or skills to protect themselves, drugs can be sold and distributed everywhere," he added.

Title: Jakarta airport, four others reopen after Anak Krakatau ash crisis
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's main airport and several other air travel hubs reopened early Tuesday after days of closure due to ash from a volcanic eruption, the Transport Ministry said.
The ministry wrote on Instagram that the airport serving the capital Jakarta and four others near the city or around the island of Java are now operating again, as the air safety crisis that left hundreds of thousands of travelers stranded subsides.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150km from Jakarta, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and a plume of volcanic ash.
Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights and leaving more than 340,000 passengers stranded, the Transport Ministry reported on Monday.
Early Tuesday the ministry posted on Instagram that Jakarta's airport and four others are up and running again.
Jakarta's main airport wrote on Instagram that "following the current volcanic eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has resumed flight operations."
Earlier, the airport closures had been repeatedly extended.
Airlines now face the daunting task of getting all the stranded passengers onto planes and to their intended destinations after days of chaos at the airports.
The other four listed as reopening include Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller Jakarta-area airport that caters to both civil and military flights, and Hussein Sastranegara in Bandung, the capital of West Java, the Transport Ministry said.
Another small airport in south Sumatra resumed operations on Monday morning. So two of the original eight are still closed.
More than 240 domestic and international flights were cancelled or delayed due to volcanic ash on Monday morning alone,  Soekarno-Hatta airport said, adding that nearly 30,000 passengers were affected.
The Transport Ministry had prepared six alternative airports as options for aircraft that were originally scheduled to land in Jakarta.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and displaced thousands.--AFP

Title: Zambry: No Malaysians will be denied place at universities
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE government commitment to expanding access to higher education means ensuring no Malaysian is denied a place at university because of their background, said Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir yesterday.
"We want to ensure access, a place of study to everyone regardless of their background, because all of them are our Malaysian children," said the higher education minister.
Zambry said he did not want to see cases where bright students from poor families were unable to pursue tertiary education due to financial hardship.
"Give them the opportunity to further their studies. Whether they are Malay, Chinese, Indian, Orang Asli, Kadazan-Dusun, Iban or otherwise, they are our children," he said, adding that such students were valuable assets to the country.
He was speaking at the presentation of undergraduate degree tuition sponsorship letters to outstanding 2025 Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) students at his ministry.
The government offered scholarships to 30 top STPM scorers, and 27 accepted.
He said Universiti Malaya accounted for six recipients who were admitted into fields including  medicine, mathematical sciences, chemical engineering, exercise science and law.
Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris took in four recipients for courses in Chinese language education, Malay language education and special education.
Zambry said many of the recipients pursuing teaching-related degrees had scored a perfect 4.0, adding that this boded well for the quality of teachers who would eventually educate the country's schoolchildren.
He urged the new undergraduates to enjoy their studies rather than view them as a source of pressure, and to treat challenges as opportunities for growth.
"Don't turn your world of learning into a world full of pressure. When there is joy in learning, you won't feel the pressure.
"You will take on any pressure or difficulty in your studies as a good challenge that makes you even better."
He also cautioned students against neglecting character and values in their pursuit of academic or professional success, saying education was ultimately about shaping good human beings, not simply obtaining a degree.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore ministers face salary debate
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SINGAPORE: The nation's ministers will discuss ministerial salaries in Parliament today, a sensitive and closely watched issue in the city-state, where political leaders are highly paid to attract talent and deter graft.
Singapore pays its political leaders the highest salaries in the world, with a junior minister earning S$1.1 million   annually and the prime minister earning S$2.2 million.
These salaries have remained unchanged since 2012, when pay was cut by 36 per cent to address public concern.
High ministerial salaries remain  a sensitive issue, with  median monthly income at S$5,775 last year.
Inflation rose to two per cent in July; the central bank expects it to remain elevated until the second half of next year.
According to data from non-profit organisation PoliticalSalaries.com (http://PoliticalSalaries.com/), the Hong Kong chief executive is the second-highest-paid political leader  globally with US$719,000, followed by the Swiss president at US$606,000.
By comparison, the British prime minister earns US$230,000, while United States President Donald Trump earns US$400,000.
Today, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing will give the government's response to a committee's recommendations on ministerial salaries.
Lawmakers will debate the issue later in the week. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangladesh dengue outbreak accelerates, straining hospitals
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
BANGLADESH'S dengue outbreak is accelerating, with 42,590 people hospitalised and 117 deaths recorded this year, as a sharp surge strains hospitals and raises fears the disease could intensify further in the coming weeks.
At least four dengue patients died and 1,558 others were hospitalised in the past 24 hours, according to health ministry data, marking the highest daily admission tally recorded so far this year.
The mosquito-borne disease, which can cause fever, severe headaches and potentially fatal complications, has spread sharply in recent weeks, reviving concerns after the country's deadliest dengue outbreak in 2023.
The rise in dengue cases has further strained a healthcare system already grappling with a nationwide measles outbreak that has killed nearly 1,000 children.
Health experts also warn that September could prove even more severe than August, which recorded the highest monthly dengue caseload of the year. —  REUTERS

Title: Over 3,000 celebrate Malaysia's colours, flavours & heritage at Malaysia Carnival in UK
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   A vibrant celebration of Malaysia's colours, flavours, heritage, and community spirit at the Malaysia Carnival 2026 drew more than 3,000 people from across the United Kingdom to the
Tun Abdul Razak Research Centre in Hertfordshire on Saturday.
Malaysian High Commissioner-Designate to the United Kingdom, Datuk Dr Azfar Mohamad Mustafar, officiated the event organised by the High Commission of Malaysia in London, delivering a message that celebrated the shared spirit, diversity, and heritage connecting Malaysians and friends of Malaysia.
In a statement, the High Commission said the carnival embodied the spirit of "Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" through the simple yet meaningful act of bringing people together.
"Food was shared, traditions were celebrated, different generations participated, and new connections were made, reflecting a vision of well-being that extends beyond prosperity to include community, inclusion, and shared joy.
"The overwhelming turnout from across the UK and beyond demonstrated the enduring appeal of Malaysian culture and the strength of the connections between Malaysia and its friends in the United Kingdom," it said.
A major highlight was the Malaysian food village, featuring more than 30 vendors serving popular dishes including nasi lemak, satay, and traditional kuih. Visitors also had the opportunity to taste durian brought from Malaysia.
The carnival also showcased Malaysia's rich performing arts, beginning with traditional percussion and folk arts such as kompang and dikir barat, followed by traditional Malaysian songs and a powerful Silat Seni Gayong demonstration that highlighted the nation's living martial arts heritage. —  BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai DPM Sihasak leaves Malaysia after Two-day working visit
Article:
SEPANG: Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sihasak Phuangketkeow departed for home after concluding his two-day working visit to Malaysia.
Chief of Ceremony at the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Rozainor Ramli was present at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1, here, to send off Sihasak who departed on a Bangkok bound commercial flight at 8.55PM.
He arrived in Malaysia yesterday for the visit, which formed part of the regular exchange of high-level visits between the two neighbouring ASEAN states.
During his visit, Sihasak met Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, with both sides discussing ways to streamline coordination among agencies from both countries, particularly on security and development in border areas as well as smuggling prevention.
Both sides also discussed a proposal to coordinate the construction of border fencing, with Thailand planning to build fences in areas Malaysia has yet to fence to avoid duplication.
On the situation in Southern Thailand, Malaysia, which has been entrusted with facilitating the peace dialogue process, would continue to assist efforts to advance the negotiations towards a more positive outcome.
In 2025, Thailand was the sixth largest trading partner globally and the second largest among ASEAN Member States, with total trade amounting to RM118.57 billion (US$27.73 billion).
From January to July 2026, bilateral trade between the two countries reached RM85.01 billion (US$21.13 billion), compared with RM66.95 billion (US$16.64 billion) during the corresponding period in 2025, reflecting the continued strong growth and potential of economic ties between the two countries. — BERNAMA

Title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
Article:
LONDON:  King Charles authorised a letter to senior British officials on Monday confirming that his youngest son Harry and Harry's wife Meghan remain non-working royals following their return to the UK.
The letter, which was shared with Harry's team and sent as guidance to senior officials in the government and military, said that after Harry and Meghan stepped down from official royal duties in 2020 they "are no longer working Members of The Royal Family."
"This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected," the letter added.
"It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. ... The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity.
"In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."
Prince Harry and his family arrived back in Britain late last month, six years after quitting royal duties and moving to the United States.
The couple had left for the U.S. in 2020, stepping down from official royal duties to chart independent careers, but they never left the headlines as Harry accused the royals of neglect, the tabloid press of ruining his life and the government of failing to provide enough security for him to ever return home. — REUTERS

Title: NST Leader: Plugging cracks in cross-border drug trade through shared intelligence
Article:
AS enforcement by Malaysia and Indonesia gets more robust, drug syndicates operate across borders and employ more complex methods to evade detection by authorities.
From using the sea and land routes  they are now flying them in, not by passengers but by pilots and other crew members. In July, a Malaysia Airlines pilot managed to slip past detectors with 26kg of ecstasy pills hidden in his luggage.
An alert Indonesian Customs officer at the Soekarno-Harta International Airport spotted the drugs and arrested him on July 29. He also tested positive for cocaine, ecstasy pills and methamphetamine.
According to a Bernama report he is said to have told the Indonesian authorities that he has been acting as a drug courier for the syndicates three times. On the first time by transporting methamphetamine to Sabah.
On the second time by transporting the same drug to Jakarta. On the two occasions he passed through without being detected. On the third occasion in July he was arrested.
This is why Malaysia's and Indonesia's narcotics crime investigation authorities are strengthening intelligence-sharing to combat cross-border drug syndicates, a disclosure made at the 14th bilateral meeting.
Malaysia's Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the meeting provided an opportunity for both parties to share their experiences in tackling drug smuggling and compare notes on syndicates' links in Malaysia and Indonesia.
Joint operations and intelligence-sharing are crucial if both countries want to combat cross-border drug smuggling. One positive sign of the information sharing is the arrest of six Malaysians who supplied the drugs to the Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta.
This is not the first time a Malaysia Airlines pilot has been involved in transporting drugs to another country. Two other pilots of the airlines were arrested in Australia.
There is a broader concern that Malaysia Airlines needs to address: how come a pilot with links to drug syndicates is still in its employment? Whatever happened to its safety and security policy?
The real test for the airlines and the airport authorities is to identify why the system didn't detect the 26kg of drugs.
We are told that all the cabin crew and others were tested. This is a pointless exercise because it is after the fact. Vulnerability must be tested and fixed earlier — not after the vulnerability fails. Was the pilot adequately screened?
Was he tested for fitness to fly? There are so many questions but very few answers. Malaysian authorities are coy when it comes to transparency. Let's not forget that it is not just the safety of the cabin crews but also that of passengers that are at risk.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Robots protest rampant AI in Poland
Article:
WARSAW: Waving flags, "chanting" slogans, and marching in circles: around 30 robots took to the streets of Warsaw on Monday to campaign for AI regulation in front of the Polish digital affairs ministry.
The protest was organised by Democratism, an initiative that, according to its website, aims to launch debate "on how AI and robotisation affect the labour market."
"The robots present here are meant to show that this technology is already a reality," Agibot A3, one of the AI-powered humanoid robots, told AFP.
Chants of: "Defend workplaces", "Time for rules", and "Don't wait, regulate" played on loudspeakers as the robots – which ranged from bipedal humanoids to dog-like quadripeds – demonstrated.
"We particularly want to address the issue of the potential replacement of people both by humanoid robots and by artificial intelligence in cognitive work," organiser Grzegorz Kulis told AFP.
"If we don't react now, we may soon have a problem," he added, emphasising the need for "rules and regulations that would serve as a shield protecting workers."
Aside from attracting the attention of several passers-by, Kulis said the use of robots was meant to show their existing capabilities and thereby, the urgency of the situation.
"These robots can already move around freely, they're already 'protesting'", he said.
The marching robots were met with a visit from Poland's Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski, who spoke to Kulis on site.
"Uncontrolled (AI) models, implemented into humanoids that will also keep evolving as robotisation moves forward, are a major problem," he said.
Kulis, who is now the CIO of a robotics company and CEO of an employment agency, served two terms on the Labor Market Council at the Ministry of Family, Labor and Social Policy.
"We feel responsible for starting to inform society about the rapid and dynamic technological changes which personally frighten us," he told AFP.
In July, Poland's conservative-nationalist president Karol Nawrocki signed into law a bill put forth by the ministry putting the EU's AI Act into practice.
It created a national authority capable of enforcing existing EU regulations, which had already formally come into force.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar congratulates TMJ, hails his sporting excellence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Tunku Ismail, Regent of Johor, after he was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026.
In a Facebook post tonight, Anwar said Tunku Ismail's outstanding performance, leadership and fighting spirit reflected his excellence as a sporting champion and a source of pride for Johor and Malaysia.
"Congratulations to His Royal Highness Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament 2026, while also leading Royal Johor to lift this prestigious title," he said.
Tunku Ismail was named MVP yesterday after delivering an outstanding performance throughout the tournament.
The accolade capped his impressive campaign as he led Royal Johor to a 10-7 victory over Temasek in the final, scoring 6 of his team's 10 goals.
The 22-goal handicap tournament, held from Sept 1 to 6, was the highest-handicap polo competition organised in Malaysia to date.
The tournament was driven by a shared vision between Tunku Ismail and Polito Pieres to position Johor as one of the leading destinations on the international polo circuit.

Title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's main airport postponed reopening on Monday after halting operations following a volcanic eruption that left hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150km from Indonesia's capital, Jakarta, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and a plume of volcanic ash.
Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights and leaving more than 340,000 passengers stranded, the transport ministry reported on Monday.
"These figures are the cumulative operational impact since Sept 5 and cover flights that have been cancelled, delayed, or diverted," the ministry said in a statement.
Italian tourist Michel Miegge was on holiday with his girlfriend and due to fly home in time for work on Tuesday, but their flight was cancelled.
"We don't have any news from the airline. We don't know if we stay another day in Jakarta or find another flight," the 32-year-old software engineer told AFP.
"I don't think it's possible now. We found a nearby hotel, but we saw that many hotels were fully booked."
Another tourist, French painter Carol Odile, said she came with a group of friends to see Komodo dragons in Flores when she was notified that her flight was cancelled.
"We are disappointed, but our group is optimistic. We hope we can go to Flores Island very soon," the 60-year-old told AFP.
Airports closed
Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport extended its closure from Monday morning to midnight.
"Due to increased eruption activity at Mount Anak Krakatau, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has suspended flight operations until 11.59pm Western Indonesia Time," the airport said in a social media post.
Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, will also remain closed.
Another small airport in south Sumatra resumed operations on Monday morning, the transport ministry said.
More than 240 domestic and international flights were cancelled or delayed due to volcanic ash on Monday morning alone, Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport said, adding that nearly 30,000 passengers were affected.
The Transport Ministry has prepared six alternative airports – including airports in East Java, Central Java, and Yogyakarta – as options for aircraft that were originally scheduled to land in Jakarta.
"We are encouraging airlines to use these airports to avoid passenger congestion, both for arrivals and departures," Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said in a statement.
Airport operators would provide free bus services for passengers who wish to fly from other airports.
Dudy said authorities extended some airport closures because the "wind direction is very dynamic" and officials "want to be absolutely sure that this volcanic ash moves away from the airport locations."
He said that the Indonesian government relaxed rules for foreign passengers who may have overstayed as a result of flight cancellations.
Threat remains high
Benjamin Foatelli, 48, a perfumer based in Jakarta for a French company, left Italy on Sunday evening for Jakarta on an Etihad flight via Abu Dhabi.
However, his connecting flight from the United Arab Emirates was delayed.
"I don't know yet if I'll be able to get back tonight, but I have everything I need to keep working so I can wait calmly for the situation to resolve," he told AFP by phone.
The probability of an eruption remained high, the country's geology agency warned.
"The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues," agency head Lana Saria said.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and displaced thousands.
