Title: Secret Assad-era Syrian nuclear reactor was almost complete
Article:
VIENNA: A near-complete nuclear reactor built secretly during the rule of toppled Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad would have been able to produce material to make nuclear weapons, the UN nuclear watchdog chief said on Monday.
Inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) last month visited two sites, one in Deir Ezzor and a second undisclosed location identified to them by Syrian authorities.
In a report seen by AFP last week, the IAEA said Syria's previous government was building a nuclear reactor.
Assad was toppled in December 2024 and the current Islamist government came to power.
IAEA head Rafael Grossi said it was "obvious that the previous government was pursuing a number of clandestine" activities.
"They didn't want the world to know what they were doing," he told reporters after opening the Vienna-based agency's quarterly board of governors meeting.
"Given the configuration, the technical features of that type of reactor, this is a reactor that is very efficient in the production of fissile material that could be used directly for the fabrication of nuclear weapons," he said, adding that building the reactor was a "very important step."
He said the reactor – which is currently being excavated – "was almost completed."
It was "very possible... that the then Syrian authorities also performed some explosions in order to... hinder any possibility of an investigation," he added.
'Missing information'
Besides the reactor under construction at the Deir Ezzor site, the IAEA found a fuel fabrication plant where nuclear fuel for the reactor was manufactured, and a location where nuclear fuel as well as uranium scrap and waste were stored.
In its report, the IAEA said it found around 73 tonnes of natural uranium metal.
Grossi has praised Damascus's "courageous decision" to report the undisclosed site.
The UN atomic watchdog had declared in 2011 that the location was "very likely" to host a nuclear reactor, adding that its information suggested it was being built with North Korean assistance.
On Monday, Grossi said it was up to the IAEA board to decide whether to close the file opened in 2011, adding that he currently had not been tasked to further investigate alleged connections to North Korea.
A draft resolution seen by AFP, expected to be submitted to the board this week for a vote, proposes closing the file.
The IAEA will continue to work with Syria to keep the material safe and report its findings, Grossi said.
The Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS), a US-based organisation specialising in nuclear proliferation, last week said questions remained.
"The new revelations (in the IAEA report) provide confirmation and new details... but they do not provide any surprises or fill in the missing information about the entire scope of the reactor and reprocessing project and Syria's cooperation with North Korea," it said.
Last month, Grossi visited the site in Deir Ezzor in the east, which has been shut for 18 years.
In 2018, Israel admitted carrying out a top-secret air raid on the site 11 years earlier.
In 2008, less than a year after the strike, US officials accused Syria of having sought to build a secret nuclear reactor and acknowledged that Israel had destroyed it in the raid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man found dead at house in Kota Belud
Article:
KOTA BELUD: A 23-year-old man was found dead at a house here today.
Kota Belud police chief Superintendent Khairul Shah Peri said police received a report on the incident at 4.20pm.
He said the man was found hanging in a room and was pronounced dead by a medical officer from the Health Ministry at Kota Belud Hospital.
"The victim was then taken to the Kota Belud Hospital forensic unit for a post-mortem, while initial investigations found no criminal element," he said in a statement tonight.
Khairul Shah said police were continuing investigations to determine the cause of death.
"Investigations are ongoing and, at this stage, the case has been classified as sudden death," he said.
He advised the public against speculating about the incident as this could affect the investigation.
Those with information are urged to contact the Kota Belud police headquarters or investigating officer Inspector Frankie Pain at 019-215 1132.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two Kota Kinabalu bus workers come to blows over passengers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A dispute over securing passengers is believed to have led to a fight between two bus company workers at the Inanam Bus Terminal in Kota Kinabalu last Friday.
The incident, which occurred at about 11.54am, involved two men aged 38 and 37 who were seen fighting without using any weapons, according to BuletinTV3.
Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said police received a report on the incident on the same day.
“Initial checks found that neither man suffered any injuries.
“Following the report, police detained both men at about 2.30pm the day before yesterday to assist with investigations,” he said in a statement.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 160 of the Penal Code for affray.
Earlier, a 29-second video showing the two men fighting at the Inanam Bus Terminal went viral on social media.

Title: Pedestrian killed in hit-and-run on LDP, Proton Saga driver flees
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — A local man in his 40s was killed after being hit by a Proton Saga in a hit-and-run incident at Kilometer 0.8 of the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP) towards Puchong early yesterday morning.
Petaling Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police received information about the incident at about 5.40am, according to Kosmo! Online.
He said initial investigations found that the incident occurred at about 4.34am when a red Proton Saga suddenly struck a pedestrian who was standing in the left lane.
“The vehicle continued driving and did not stop after the incident,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the victim, who suffered serious injuries, was pronounced dead at the scene.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police urged anyone who witnessed the incident or was at the scene to come forward at the nearest police station or contact traffic investigating officer Inspector M. Sivam at 017-3290749 to assist with investigations.
Members of the public can also contact the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters operations room at 03-79662222.

Title: Malaysia Airlines flight to Jeddah diverted to Chennai over suspected engine problem
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai, India on Monday after a suspected problem with one of its engines, according to Indian media reports.
According to national news agency Bernama, citing a report by the
Times of India
, flight MH156, carrying 186 passengers, made an emergency landing at Chennai Airport before the aircraft was moved to a parking bay, while passengers were provided accommodation at the airport.
“There was a technical problem involving engine number two.
“The airline and the relevant technical teams are conducting further assessment of the aircraft and the issue,” an airport spokesperson told news agency PTI.
The Hindu, citing Airports Authority of India (AAI) officials, reported that the flight departed Kuala Lumpur at 3.30pm before the pilot suspected an engine malfunction and requested permission to land in Chennai.

Title: Firefighter swims 50m to rescue man who jumped from Kuala Selangor bridge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Quick action by firefighters saved a man who jumped from the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah 5 Bridge in Kuala Selangor last night.
According to Kosmo! Online, the 44-year-old man was rescued at about 9.15pm after a firefighter swam 50 metres from the riverbank to reach him.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Division assistant director Asrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 8.05pm, with five firefighters from the Kuala Selangor Fire and Rescue Station involved in the operation.
He said the firefighters, who arrived five minutes later, immediately began the rescue operation.
“The victim was rescued by a firefighter who swam 50 metres towards his location.
“The man did not suffer any injuries and was subsequently handed over to Health Ministry personnel and police for further action,” he said today.

Title: Fire at FRIM Bidor burns 2.42ha forest area, operation resumes this morning
Article:
IPOH, Sept 8 — About 2.42 hectares of forest area at the Forest Research Institute of Malaysia (FRIM) in Bidor caught fire in an incident yesterday evening.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said his department received a call about the fire at 5.42 pm before a team of personnel from the Bidor Fire and Rescue Station was rushed to the location.
He said the operation was carried out using a 700-foot jet stream with two jets and a transport pump which sourced water from a nearby pond.
“The operation continued last night with a change of personnel at the location.
“The fire was put under control and only 15 per cent of the burning area remains,” he said in a statement.
He said the operation was suspended at 12 last night due to safety factors and the condition of the fire that would not spread.
The operation resumed this morning. — Bernama

Title: Maritime industry expert urges clearer timelines for probes, says prolonged uncertainty hurts businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan has called for clear timelines to be set for investigations into alleged corruption and other misconduct, saying prolonged probes without clear updates could create uncertainty for affected parties.
He said enforcement agencies must be given sufficient time to conduct thorough investigations, but there should also be a mechanism to ensure complainants are informed of the progress and outcome of their reports within a reasonable period.
Jeyenderan said this was particularly important in cases involving businesses and matters with potential implications for government revenue, regulatory compliance and the country’s maritime industry.
“I received auto-generated emails and SMS messages from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) stating that the case was under action. But since June until now, I have not received any written explanation from MACC.
“The prolonged uncertainty had badly affected the businesses involved, particularly in making commercial decisions and planning operations,” he said in a statement today.
With more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, Jeyenderan said the lack of a formal written update had made it difficult for him to understand the current status of the investigation and whether any further information or documents were required from his side.
The businessman said he respected the MACC and its investigative process, and had cooperated fully by providing documents and information requested by its officers.
The report was lodged on June 5 over alleged discrepancies between bills of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, Johor, involving transactions said to be worth millions of ringgit.
He had previously said the matter could have wider implications if the allegations were substantiated, including possible effects on government revenue, regulatory compliance and confidence in Malaysia’s maritime and petroleum sectors.
Jeyenderan said his concern was not to interfere with or pressure investigators, but to ensure that investigations were conducted efficiently and that affected parties were given appropriate clarity.
“Setting a timeline does not mean rushing an investigation or compromising due process. It is about ensuring accountability while allowing investigators sufficient time to establish the facts,” he said.
He said clear timelines, regular communication and proper documentation of investigation outcomes would help strengthen public confidence in enforcement agencies, particularly in cases involving allegations of corruption, abuse of power or revenue leakage.
Jeyenderan said a transparent approach would also provide greater certainty to businesses and industry players while ensuring that enforcement agencies retained the independence and discretion necessary to conduct their investigations.
MACC had previously informed him that the report had been received and referred to its Information Assessment Committee, with the investigation subsequently proceeding.
Jeyenderan had also said he was informed that the probe remained ongoing.

Title: Two men with 65 criminal records between them arrested over 12 house-breaking cases
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Sept 8 — Police arrested two men in a raid in Teluk Kemang on Sept 3 to assist in investigations into 12 house-breaking cases in Negeri Sembilan, Perak and Kedah.
Port Dickson police chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said both suspects, aged 24 and 34, were picked up around 4 pm by the district Criminal Investigation Division.
He said background checks revealed that the first suspect has 54 prior criminal records and is wanted in two outstanding cases, while the second suspect has 11 prior criminal records.
“Investigations revealed that both are suspected of being involved in four house-breaking cases in Negeri Sembilan, three in Kedah and five in Perak,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said police also seized several items including bags, identification cards, foreign currency, fishing rods, a laptop, mobile phones and a vehicle. Also confiscated were approximately 6.8 grammes of drugs.
Ahmad Afiq said both suspects have been remanded until Sept 9 to facilitate investigations under Section 457 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Thailand’s Sihasak departs Malaysia after two-day visit focused on border security, development and smuggling
Article:
SEPANG, Sept 8 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sihasak Phuangketkeow departed for home after concluding his two-day working visit to Malaysia.
Chief of Ceremony at the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Rozainor Ramli was present at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1, here, to send off Sihasak who departed on a Bangkok bound commercial flight at 8.55PM last night.
He arrived in Malaysia on Sunday for the visit, which formed part of the regular exchange of high-level visits between the two neighbouring Asean states.
During his visit, Sihasak met Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, with both sides discussing ways to streamline coordination among agencies from both countries, particularly on security and development in border areas as well as smuggling prevention.
Both sides also discussed a proposal to coordinate the construction of border fencing, with Thailand planning to build fences in areas Malaysia has yet to fence to avoid duplication.
On the situation in Southern Thailand, Malaysia, which has been entrusted with facilitating the peace dialogue process, would continue to assist efforts to advance the negotiations towards a more positive outcome.
In 2025, Thailand was the sixth largest trading partner globally and the second largest among Asean Member States, with total trade amounting to RM118.57 billion (US$27.73 billion).
From January to July 2026, bilateral trade between the two countries reached RM85.01 billion (US$21.13 billion), compared with RM66.95 billion (US$16.64 billion) during the corresponding period in 2025, reflecting the continued strong growth and potential of economic ties between the two countries. — Bernama

Title: Anwar congratulates Tunku Mahkota Ismail after Royal Johor triumphs, Regent named MVP of Johor Super Crown Polo tournament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his congratulations to Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026.
In a Facebook post last night, he said Tunku Mahkota Ismail’s outstanding performance, leadership and fighting spirit highlighted His Royal Highness’ excellence as a sporting champion who is a source of pride not only to the people of Johor but also to all Malaysians.
“Congratulations to His Royal Highness Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, on being named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament 2026, while also leading Royal Johor to lift this prestigious title,” he said.
Tunku Mahkota Ismail was named the MVP of JSCPT 2026 yesterday after delivering an outstanding performance throughout the prestigious tournament.
The MVP accolade capped Tunku Mahkota Ismail’s impressive performance as he led Royal Johor to a 10-7 victory over Temasek in the final, contributing six of his team’s 10 goals.
The 22-goal handicap tournament, held from Sept 1 to 6, was the highest-handicap polo competition organised in Malaysia to date.
The tournament was driven by a shared vision between Tunku Mahkota Ismail and Polito Pieres to position Johor as one of the leading destinations on the international polo circuit. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh: Transport problems threatening school attendance of 989 Labuan students, 437 to get aid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A total of 989 students from 25 schools in the Federal Territory of Labuan have been identified as facing school attendance issues, with transportation among the main contributing factors.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, in a post on Facebook, said that, as a start, 437 students across six schools would receive assistance through the Student School Transportation Facility in the Federal Territory of Labuan.
She said the initiative was being implemented through collaboration between the Federal Territories Department and Labuan Corporation, the Labuan Federal Territory Education Department, schools, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) and the industry, particularly the Labuan Mini Bus Operators Association.
Hannah said the collaboration aimed to ensure that transportation issues would no longer hinder students from attending school.
“There are children who want to go to school. What stands in their way is not a lack of ambition, but the journey to reach the place where they build their future.
“Their future should not be stalled simply because getting to school is difficult,” she said in a Facebook post. — Bernama

Title: Decomposed body of unidentified man found in overgrown area in Bukit Jelutong
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 8 — Police have confirmed the discovery of the decomposed body of a man in an overgrown area near Jalan Persiaran Balairong U8, Bukit Jelutong, here yesterday.
Shah Alam district police chief ACP Sarudin Samah said police received a public report at about 2.45 pm and sent a team to the scene to investigate.
He said police were unable to identify the deceased as no identification documents were found at the scene.
“An examination of the deceased’s body could not be carried out due to its condition. Based on the state of the body, the deceased is believed to have died more than a week ago,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Sarudin said the body had been sent to the Forensic Medicine Department at Al-Sultan Abdullah Hospital, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Puncak Alam, for a post-mortem examination scheduled for 2 pm today.
Sarudin said the case has been classified as a sudden death and urged anyone with information to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Fildza Che Ibrahim at 016-953 7372 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Six hikers safely rescued after going missing during Trans Gerah expedition in Gunung Gerah
Article:
GERIK, Sept 8 — Six individuals who were found safe after participating in the Trans Gerah expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, were safely brought out by the search and rescue (SAR) team last night.
The Gerik district police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the rescue team brought all the hikers out of the Kem Kulim and arrived at Kampung Lelar at around 8.45 pm.
“All the victims are currently receiving treatment at the Pos Kemar Klinik Kesihatan and are in good condition without any injuries,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said all the victims had previously gathered at Kem Kulim with the rescue team before continuing their journey to Pos Kemar.
He said that the operation to bring out the victims was also assisted by mountain guides from Perak and Kelantan, involving 10 members.
Previously, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, along with their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were reported missing after climbing the mountain on Aug 29.
They were reported to have failed to exit the forest by the scheduled date, which was Sept 3, and family members filed a police report on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Police open probe into Abdul Hadi’s claim US offered to help topple BN govt in 2014
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have opened an investigation paper into PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s claim that he was once offered cooperation by the United States (US) to topple the Barisan Nasional (BN) government in 2014.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the case is being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code for offences related to statements conducive to public mischief.
He said investigations are also being carried out under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for the improper use of network facilities or network services.
“To date, PDRM has received 12 police reports regarding the issue and statements from 12 witnesses have been recorded. Abdul Hadi’s statement will also be taken in the near future to complete the investigation,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Kumar advised the public not to make any speculation that could interfere with the ongoing investigation process, urging them to use social media platforms responsibly and to avoid making any statements that could threaten public order and safety.
Abdul Hadi previously claimed that several PAS leaders were once invited to a meeting with the US Embassy when then-US President Barack Obama visited Malaysia in 2014, with the foreign side allegedly offering assistance to topple the government at the time.
Yesterday, the US Embassy here stated on its Facebook page that the country had never attempted to determine Malaysia’s political leadership and described any statements to the contrary as false. — Bernama

Title: Nepal floods: What we know so far about unaccounted Malaysians and Malaysia’s relief efforts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Nearly two weeks after devastating floods struck parts of Nepal and the Nepal-Tibet border, rescue and recovery efforts are continuing, with Malaysians among those still unaccounted for.
To date, at least 1,300 people have been killed and more than 5,500 remain missing across Nepal and China’s Tibet region.
Among the missing are more than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries, including tourists and pilgrims who had travelled to Tibet to visit Mount Kailash.
Here is what we know so far about the Malaysians still unaccounted for and Malaysia’s response.
Still missing
On August 26, a torrent of water, mud and rocks swept through communities in Nepal and China’s Tibet Autonomous Region following a glacial collapse, causing an estimated Rs387.54 billion (RM10.3 billion) in damage, according to preliminary findings by the Nepalese government.
Immediately after the disaster, Wisma Putra initially confirmed that 55 Malaysian nationals reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu as uncontactable due to severe disruptions in communications and electricity networks.
On August 29, the ministry further confirmed 36 Malaysians were reported as uncontactable in areas affected by telecommunications disruptions in China.
As of September 7, however, the ministry’s official records show that 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable, with verification efforts continuing through diplomatic channels with the Chinese government to determine whether reports of Malaysians in Nepal overlap with those in Tibet.
Among those reported uncontactable were Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa and eight other members of his expedition team, including Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul.
The group was reported missing after the four-wheel-drive vehicle they were using during an expedition to Everest Base Camp was believed to have been affected by flooding while travelling through a valley in Rasuwa.
Others missing include 49 Malaysian citizens across three tour groups who travelled to Nepal for trekking and religious activities, including Hindu pilgrimages.
Malaysian relief
On September 5, the National Disaster Management Agency deployed an 11-member Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to Nepal to assist in ongoing rescue and disaster relief operations.
The 11-member team will use high-capacity drones and specialised equipment to support operations led by the Nepalese authorities in areas requiring technical expertise and specialised operational capabilities.
In Malaysia, preparations for victim identification are also underway, including the collection and analysis of DNA samples from next of kin by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Department of Chemistry Malaysia, in coordination with the ministry.
Other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster, including a five-member team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance.
Mercy Malaysia has also deployed a humanitarian assessment team to Nepal to assess ground conditions and identify urgent needs, including emergency shelter, food, clean water, sanitation and healthcare.
In addition, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim also pledged US$1 million in humanitarian aid to assist flood victims and support post-disaster recovery efforts.

Title: MAHB: 41 flights to Jakarta cancelled following Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A total of 41 flights to Jakarta (CGK) were cancelled at airports nationwide today following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption, according to Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB).
It said the cancellations involved flights scheduled between 6.45 am and 11.55 pm today.
“The highest number of cancellations was recorded at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), with 30 flights, comprising 20 at Terminal 1 and 10 at Terminal 2,” it said.
The airport operator said that Penang International Airport recorded seven cancellations, followed by Subang Airport with two, while Kuching International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport recorded one cancellation each.
No cancellations were recorded at Kota Bharu Airport.
The cancellations followed the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption affected flight operations. — Bernama

Title: Four-month old baby dies after found unconscious at Dungun childcare centre
Article:
DUNGUN,  Sept 7 — A four-month-old baby girl died after being found unconscious at a childcare centre in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah (AMBS) near here today.
Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the incident at 3.41 pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the baby had been dropped off at the centre by her mother at about 8 am in good health.
“At about 10 am, staff at the centre found the victim unconscious after she had slept and been fed milk.
“She was taken to Durian Mas Health Clinic before being referred to Dungun Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
Nik Ab Halim said medical personnel at the hospital conducted examinations and resuscitation efforts, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but the baby was pronounced dead at about 12.45 pm.
He said no visible physical injuries were found during an initial examination of the body.
“However, the exact cause of death has yet to be determined, and a post-mortem examination will be conducted,” he said.
He added that police had identified the two caregivers on duty at the time and would record their statements, along with those of the victim’s parents and other relevant witnesses.
Police will also obtain medical reports and professional opinions as part of the investigation.
The police have opened an investigation under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 to determine whether there were elements of negligence or abandonment while the victim was under the care of the childcare centre. — Bernama

Title: Police: Six missing Gunung Trans Gerah hikers contacted, safe for now
Article:
IPOH, Sept 7 — Six individuals, including two children, who were reported missing while trekking along the Gunung Trans Gerah trail in Lojing, Gua Musang, have managed to make contact this afternoon and reported that they are safe.
Gerik police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said information regarding the group’s condition was received at about 5.30 pm today after a family member managed to contact one of the mountain guides accompanying the group.
“We can only confirm that the victims have been contacted, and they informed their family members that they are safe.
“However, we have not found the victims yet because they are still at the climbing location, and the rescue team will move to meet them before bringing them out either today or tomorrow, as they are believed to be within the Perak area,” he said when contacted today.
He added that the exact condition of all the victims, including the possibility of any injuries, cannot be confirmed until the rescue team successfully locates them.
Abdul Samad said the method for extracting the group - whether by land or air - will be determined based on their condition and location after the SAR team manages to meet the victims.
“If conditions permit, we will see whether to use a helicopter or land routes; we will assess the situation when the rescue team meets the hikers later. The SAR process will only end after all the victims are successfully brought down,” he said.
Previously, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, along with their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were reported missing after trekking the mountain on Aug 29.
They were reported to have failed to exit the forest by their scheduled date of Sept 3, and family members lodged a police report yesterday.
Meanwhile, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said smoke signals detected during an aerial survey by a JBPM helicopter helped the SAR team estimate the location of the six missing hikers in the forested area of Pos Kemar here.
Based on the aerial survey, the location of the hikers was estimated to be about an hour’s journey from Kem Kulim. The JBPM Mi-17 aircraft from the Subang Air Base, which arrived at Pos Kemar at 4.30 pm today, brought 11 SAR personnel comprising five JBPM personnel, four Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel, one Forestry Department officer and one mountain guide.
“The SAR team was also assisted by 14 Malaysian Mountain Guides (MGM), who entered through the hiking trail, bringing the total number of SAR personnel to 25,” she said in a statement today.
Sayani said based on assessments and discussions between JBPM and the Forestry Department, as well as information from the hikers’ last short message service (SMS) on Sept 1, the group was believed to have used the route via Gunung Bieh, Gunung Sepat, Gunung Belatoh, Kampung Agek, Gunung Bongok and subsequently Pos Kemar.
The Forestry Department also received information at 5.15 pm today regarding a message from the hikers informing that all of them had arrived safely at Gunung Bongok.
“The SAR team is now moving to meet the missing hikers in the area, and they are expected to regroup at Kem Kulim tonight. The decision on whether they will be brought out tonight or spend the night at Kem Kulim will depend on their condition and the situation at the location,” she said.
Sayani said the estimated journey for the SAR team, together with the hikers, from Kem Kulim to Pos Kemar was between three and four hours. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians urged to register on Foreign Ministry’s E-Konsular as precaution, though not mandatory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Recent developments around the world, arising from natural disasters and geopolitical situations, have increased the need for Malaysians to register with the Foreign Affairs Ministry’s
e-Konsular
system to provide information on their whereabouts.
For instance, when major floods occurred in Nepal last month, information on Malaysians there was obtained only from their relatives back home and travel agencies used by Malaysians travelling to the country.
The
e-Konsular
system helps Malaysian diplomatic missions around the world provide assistance more quickly in the event of an emergency.
Registration can be done at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my/login
or by downloading the e-Konsular application via a QR code.
According to the
ekonsular.kln.gov.my
website, the registration is intended to systematically record the whereabouts of Malaysians overseas.
Consular assistance for Malaysians abroad is one of the efforts by the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, to safeguard their welfare in all circumstances.
It covers cases involving the death, detention or disappearance of Malaysians abroad; deposits of money by family members for those requiring consular assistance; as well as other disasters and emergencies.
A survey of posts on the social media platform Threads found that many Malaysian users shared their experiences registering with
e-Konsular
while abroad.
Threads user
icecoffeeonearth
suggested that Malaysians email the Malaysian Embassy in the country they are visiting if the
e-Konsular
application cannot be accessed.
Another Threads user,
solehahtravel
, said that although registration is not mandatory, registering with
e-Konsular
would at least make it easier for Malaysians to deal with the relevant authorities.
“Misfortune can happen without warning…,” said the Threads user solehahtravel. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia deploying DNA experts to identify disaster victims, pending Nepal’s go-ahead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept  7 —Malaysia is awaiting approval from the Nepalese government to deploy deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) experts to assist in identifying the bodies of disaster victims in the country.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia had submitted a request to deploy the experts, with the DNA identification process expected to begin after search and rescue (SAR) operations conclude.
He said the expertise was needed to match DNA samples taken from recovered bodies with samples provided by the families of Malaysian citizens who remain missing.
“There are bodies that have been recovered but were immediately buried due to a lack of adequate facilities.
“We need DNA to match against the DNA samples from the families of the Malaysian citizens. The process will be carried out once the search and rescue (SAR) operation concludes,” he told a press conference following a luncheon held in conjunction with the working visit of Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow here today.
Last Saturday, Mohamad announced that DNA samples had been successfully collected from the next of kin of the 55 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal.
Meanwhile, he said the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), which is currently en route to the affected areas, would assist the Nepalese authorities in efforts to locate the missing victims.
Mohamad expressed hope that the team’s presence would contribute to search and recovery efforts for those still classified as missing.
Yesterday, the SMART MAS01 team, deployed as part of the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission to Nepal, arrived safely at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu at noon local time.
The National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) said the team completed arrival procedures and mission protocols by 4.30 pm local time, including logistics clearance and personnel manifest verification.
The team comprises 11 SMART members and officers carrying 12.4 tonnes of SAR equipment, including rescue gear, detection tools, communication systems, high-capacity drones and specialised tunnel rescue equipment, as well as a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne truck. — Bernama

Title: Elderly man remanded four days for slashing wife’s hand
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 7 — An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife’s right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here today has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations.
The remand order for the man, who is in his 70s, was issued by the Kota Tinggi Magistrate’s Court to facilitate further investigations under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a weapon.
Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at about 9.30 pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high.
The suspect, who was intoxicated, then allegedly attacked the victim with the machete.
He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.
She is reported to be in stable condition, he added. — Bernama

Title: Police tracking down 10 suspects to assist in murder, gang fight in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — Police are tracking down 10 men to assist in the investigation of two separate fight cases in Taman Alam Megah and Taman Sri Muda here last month.
Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said of that number, seven men are wanted to assist in the investigation of a fight in Taman Alam Megah that resulted in the death of a 23-year-old local man on Aug 25.
Meanwhile, three others are wanted in connection with a case where a man was attacked with a machete and threatened with an object resembling a firearm in Taman Sri Muda last month.
“All of the individuals involved are aged between 23 and 46, and those still at large are wanted to assist in ongoing investigations,” he said at a press conference at the Selangor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said following both cases, police conducted a series of raids in Shah Alam, as well as Lenga and Iskandar Puteri, Johor, between Aug 14 and 28.
As a result of the raids, police successfully arrested 21 local men aged between 23 and 46, and also seized various weapons including seven machetes, two cable cutters, nine cars, and three motorcycles.
“Out of the 21 arrested, eight male suspects have been charged in court under Sections 302 and 149 of the Penal Code, while another four men were charged under Section 148 of the same act,” he said.
He said checks also revealed that the victim who died in the Taman Alam Megah case had six past criminal records related to drug offences.
Meanwhile, Shazeli said police do not rule out the possibility that both cases are linked to elements of gangsterism, but involving different factions.
“At the early stage, we believe the case involving the death stems from a turf war, while the other resulted from a misunderstanding.
“Police will not compromise with any individuals involved in gangsterism and will ensure they are all brought to court,” he said.
On Aug 27, Shazeli confirmed that the fight incident in Taman Alam Megah involved a group of individuals resulting in the death of a man, suspected to stem from rivalry between two secret society groups.
Eight men, including two brothers who are members of a secret society group, were hauled to the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court on Sept 4 to face murder charges.
In a separate incident on Aug 13, a local man was seriously injured after reportedly being slashed with a machete during a fight near a petrol station in Taman Sri Muda at around 11 am. — Bernama

Title: Housing Ministry: Check Teduh to check project, developer information before buying property
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The public, particularly prospective homebuyers, are encouraged to check information on developers and housing projects through the TEDUH portal and mobile application before making a purchase decision to reduce the risk of encountering problems later.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said TEDUH, developed by the National Housing Department (JPN), is a one-stop platform providing access to information such as developers’ licence status, advertising permit and developer’s licence (APDL), project progress and information related to private housing projects.
“Through the #TEDUHBersama campaign, the ministry aims to cultivate the practice of ‘check before you buy’ among the public, particularly prospective homebuyers, as an initial step to reduce the risk of dealing with unlicensed developers or making purchase decisions without knowing the actual status of a project,” the ministry said in a statement.
It added that the portal also provides facilities to check the status of private housing projects, including projects categorised as delayed, troubled or abandoned, as well as approved selling prices.
Users can also check certain approvals issued by the government, including extensions of time (EOT), verify the authenticity of related documents and submit housing development complaints to JPN for review and further action.
JPN director-general Dr Tan Awang Besar, in the same statement, said the public was advised to conduct checks before purchasing a house as it was one of the biggest financial commitments in a person’s life.
“This simple step is important to help buyers obtain accurate information, make decisions with greater confidence and reduce the risk of encountering problems later,” he said.
TEDUH was launched on Aug 11, 2017, and has since been progressively enhanced as a more comprehensive, transparent and user-friendly housing reference platform.
According to KPKT, the TEDUH portal recorded more than 45 million visitors in total as of August.
The public can access the TEDUH Portal via
teduh.kpkt.gov.my
or use the TEDUH mobile application. — Bernama

Title: Over 26,000 new undergraduates to benefit from RM1,500 PTPTN advance payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) continues to strengthen the nation’s higher education empowerment agenda by offering Loan Advance Payments (WPP) totaling RM1,500 to eligible new students to help cover part of the initial preparation costs for admission to public universities and polytechnics.
In a statement, PTPTN said the RM39.7 million scheme benefits 26,457 students entering bachelor’s degree programmes at public universities and polytechnics for the September 2026 intake.
“The WPP is available to Malaysian citizens who opted into the scheme when applying to public higher education institutions via UPUOnline or university websites.
“In addition, applicants’ parents or guardians must be recipients of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and meet the specified eligibility criteria,” according to the statement.
From WPP’s introduction in 1999 until July 31, more than 1 million students have benefited from the initiative, with an allocation totaling RM1.48 billion, it said.
The agency, which operates under the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE), said applicants can check their offers via the myPTPTN mobile app and collect the cash at Bank Islam branches nationwide starting Sept 4 by presenting their WPP offer letter and MyKad.
“The WPP is valid for two months, from Sept 4 to Nov 3 (Tuesday),” it said, noting that third-party collection is not permitted.
Recently, PTPTN also reached out to students receiving the WPP offer through home visits in Tasek Gelugor, Penang, followed by the WPP handover ceremony for the Bukit Gelugor area, officiated by PTPTN Chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim.
According to the statement, Norliza said in her speech that PTPTN remains committed to strengthening the higher education agenda by ensuring that access to education financing continues to be empowered and can be enjoyed by all layers of society regardless of background and socio-economic status.
“In line with that aspiration, PTPTN’s WPP is among the strategic initiatives implemented to provide early financial support to students, thereby helping to ease the financial burden on families in making preparations and meeting basic needs before students begin studies at public universities and polytechnics,” she said.
PTPTN also said that students who wish to apply for loans can submit applications online via the myPTPTN application during the application period set by each public university and polytechnic, to ensure applications are processed and approved accordingly.
PTPTN said students must have a National Education Savings Scheme (Simpan SSPN) account, which can be opened through the myPTPTN application, urging them to refer to the Student Affairs Division of their respective universities and polytechnics or contact PTPTN if they have any questions.
It said additional details on loan advances and educational financing can be obtained from the myPTPTN digital application for easier, faster, and safer services. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia rail link: ECRL passenger fares to be known by year-end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Passenger fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) have not been finalised and an official announcement will be made by the end of this year, said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL).
MRL said in a statement on the ECRL Facebook page today that a recently recirculated information on social media regarding the passenger fares is inaccurate and has never been verified by any authority.
The company said the official passenger fares for the ECRL will only be announced by the Ministry of Transport Malaysia once the relevant evaluation and approval processes are finalised.
MRL advised the public against making any assumptions or conclusions based on unverified information, and to instead refer to announcements made through official channels of the Ministry of Transport, MRL, and ECRL.
"The ECRL fares will be determined after taking into account the public interest, user affordability, as well as the value and quality of services to be offered,” it said.
MRL said that once operational, travel time between Kota Bharu and Gombak is expected to take around four hours, Kuala Terengganu to Gombak about three hours, and Kuantan to Gombak approximately one hour and 35 minutes.
"The ECRL not only offers a new transport option for the public, but will also transform mobility between the East Coast and the Klang Valley,” it said.
The first phase of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Gombak is expected to begin operations this December. — Bernama

Title: Minden air quality hits unhealthy level as API rises to 142, says Penang exco
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — Air quality in parts of Penang island reached an unhealthy level today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading climbing to 142 at 3pm.
Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the Minden air-quality monitoring station on the island began recording unhealthy readings at 9am.
“The reading continued to rise, reaching 142 at 3pm,” he said in a statement today.
He said the station recorded readings of between 82 and 142 throughout the day.
Meanwhile, monitoring stations in Seberang Perai, Seberang Jaya and Balik Pulau recorded moderate readings of between 55 and 91.
Minden was the only one of Penang’s four monitoring stations to record unhealthy air quality.
Sundarajoo said Penang’s air quality had generally remained at good to moderate levels between September 4 and 6.
He said preliminary information from the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre showed that 737 hotspots were recorded in Sumatra and another 540 in Kalimantan during the period.
Hotspots were also detected in several Malaysian states.
“The increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicates more significant fire activity in the region,” he said.
However, Sundarajoo said hotspot numbers alone could not determine Penang’s air quality.
He said the impact on the state depended on factors such as wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall distribution.
“Intermittent rain had helped keep Penang’s air quality within good to moderate levels during the monitoring period,” he said.
PM₁₀ was identified as the dominant pollutant, although its concentration remained at a moderate level.
He advised the public to monitor official API readings for their respective areas through the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
He also urged the public not to rely on unverified information or social media posts.
He advised the public to avoid open burning, including burning rubbish, dried leaves and agricultural waste, and to report such activities immediately.
Children, senior citizens and those with respiratory conditions should reduce strenuous outdoor activities if API readings rise.
The public should also reduce the time spent outdoors, keep doors and windows closed, and wear suitable face masks if air quality worsens.
Sundarajoo said the public should avoid activities that could worsen air pollution and reduce unnecessary vehicle use.
He encouraged residents to use public transport, carpool or choose more sustainable ways of travelling.
He said the Department of Environment and other relevant agencies will continue monitoring air quality and regional hotspots.

Title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS.
PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS.
He said PKR nonetheless keeps a close watch on shifting political dynamics from time to time,
Harian Metro
reported.
“So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.
“We discussed national issues seriously, but there was no political chit-chat during the Cabinet meeting.
“We'll see how things unfold, this is a party matter. I can only confirm there is no turmoil in the Cabinet at this point,” Chang was quoted as saying at a press conference after the National Science Challenge Prime Minister's Cup final here.
He was responding to Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s earlier statement that
PH would not be invited to Umno’s assembly this week, as PAS had already been invited.
Zahid said Umno would focus on the pros and cons of cooperation rather than finalising any coalition arrangement ahead of the 16th general election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier said the decision to invite PAS’ top leadership was agreed upon at the party’s supreme council meeting.

Title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case.
“We estimate it may take three to four months for us to obtain the findings of the investigation. This is because we need technical reports from several agencies involved,” he told a news conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters in Shah Alam.
He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.
“Police have taken statements from the staff operating the ride, victims and medical officers,” Shazeli said.
The ride accident occurred at about 9pm on August 22 and involved 22 local and foreign visitors aged between 11 and 44, with no deaths reported.
Selangor DOSH previously said a preliminary investigation found the roller coaster had been operating normally before a “sliding failure” about 200m from the disembarkation point triggered its automatic emergency braking system, causing it to stop abruptly.
As of September 2, all visitors treated and placed under observation at hospitals had been discharged.
The roller coaster remains closed pending completion of the investigation.

Title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday.
Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend.
“There's give and take. If they invite us, we invite them,” he was quoted as saying by
Utusan Malaysia
today.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier announced that the decision to invite PAS had been made in a consensus during a supreme council meeting.
Zahid said the Umno assembly this year would not decide on cooperation with any coalition, particularly ahead of the 16th general election.
He said discussions would instead focus on the potential benefits and risks to Umno and Barisan Nasional should any such cooperation be formed.
“Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.
“I don't want to unite Malay parties, but as a whole, Malays want Malay unity to be realised,” he was quoted as saying.

Title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Some villages in Nepal have been so completely devastated by the floods that there is no sign they ever existed, according to Malaysian relief volunteers who have seen the destruction first-hand.
Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur.
“The damage is very severe. In some villages, there isn’t even one house left. If someone went there for the first time, they would think there was no village there,” he told
Harian Metro
today.
“In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. In some places, there is no trace of any houses at all.”
Even concrete buildings were not spared, with only about 20 per cent of such structures still standing in some settlements, he said.
“Most of these concrete buildings were also swept away,” Vivegananthan recounted.
Accumulated sludge lines the Trishuli riverbank after flash floods at Trishuli Bazar in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 5, 2026, as survivors struggle to rebuild homes destroyed by the disaster. — AFP pic
Survivors have since been moved away from the worst-hit areas, with many evacuated to Kathmandu and Nuwakot and housed in schools and halls on higher ground.
Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.
In Nuwakot alone, 19 such shelters have been established, he said.
Based on discussions with local authorities and assessments on the ground, food supplies at the shelters were adequate, but survivors needed other forms of assistance.
Mercy Malaysia’s three-member team will remain in Nepal for about 10 days to assess how best to support those who survived the disaster.
Mercy Malaysia’s Rapid Assessment Team assesses the extent of the flood devastation and health needs in Trishuli Dhunge Bazar, Bidur, as relief efforts continue in Nepal. — Picture from Facebook/MERCY Malaysia
Vivegananthan stressed that the team was not involved in search and rescue operations but was focused on helping survivors rebuild their lives.
“We are not involved in search and rescue. We are here to help those who survived,” he said.
Among the assistance provided are medicines, cooking equipment and toys for children, which are being channelled through Nepali authorities, including the country’s Health Ministry.
“The assistance we provide is aimed at helping them continue their lives as best as possible so they can return to normal,” Vivegananthan said.

Title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported.
“Not long now. I said four Fridays the other day, but now there are only two Fridays left,” he was quoted saying during at a community programme in Sungai Udang here.
His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.
